member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Audio.FliteTtsService
member.summary: Synthesizes text to speech with Flite on a worker thread and plays it through a single hidden AudioSource on the main thread. One synthesis runs at a time with a single utterance queued behind the one playing; calls past that are dropped, and the service becomes a no-op if the native library is unavailable.

member.summary: The native Flite wrapper to P/Invoke; __Internal on iOS, which forbids dynamically loaded plugins.

member.summary: The maximum input length synthesized; longer text is truncated to bound native work.

member.summary: Linear gain applied to synthesized samples; Flite's kal16 output is quiet relative to other game audio.

member.name: F:Assets.Scripts.Audio.FliteTtsService.PlaybackTailMarginSeconds
member.summary: How long a clip is kept past its dsp end before destruction, so clock granularity can't shave the final samples.

member.name: F:Assets.Scripts.Audio.FliteTtsService.MaxOutstandingUtterances
member.summary: Max utterances live at once: one playing or synthesizing plus one queued; calls past this drop silently.

member.summary: The source that plays synthesized utterances.

member.summary: Localizes the text of a contract that a level authored into its game state.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Career.CareerUtilities.BuildRequirementKey(System.Xml.Linq.XElement,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Builds a contract-relative locale key for a requirement XML attribute.
member.remarks: The key is composed of the contract id, a dot-separated path of element segments from the <Contract> root down to the target element (the wrapping <Requirements> element is skipped), and a field name suffix derived from the attribute name. Each path segment uses the element's natural identifier (first matching attribute among id, name, locationId, tutorialId, payloadId, event) when present, or falls back to the element's local name plus an index when same-name siblings exist. Returns null if the element is not under a <Contract> root or required inputs are missing.
member.param: The contract id (the id attribute of the enclosing <Contract>).
The locale key suffix corresponding to the XML attribute (e.g. Description).
member.returns: The composed locale key, or null if it cannot be built.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Career.CareerUtilities.BuildAttributeLocaleKey(System.Xml.Linq.XElement,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Builds the locale key for a localizable contract attribute, or null when the attribute is not localizable.
member.param: The XML element the attribute belongs to.
member.returns: The locale key, or null.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Career.CareerUtilities.BuildRequirementSegment(System.Xml.Linq.XElement)
member.summary: Builds the path segment for a single requirement element. Uses the first non-empty "natural id" attribute if present, otherwise the element's local name. When multiple siblings produce the same base segment (e.g. two same-named elements without an id attribute, or two tutorial blocks sharing the same tutorialId) the segment is suffixed with the element's index among those colliding siblings.
member.param: The element to build a segment for.
member.returns: The path segment.

member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.FixQuadDistortionScript
member.summary: Script for fixing texture distortion on quads by introducing a q parameter into the UVs of the mesh that the part shader uses to fix the distortion. This will cause the part mesh UV set 0 to be changed to a Vector4. This script also looks at the x coord of UV set 1 to determine which vertices should be updated to use the q parameter. If the x coord is less than -0.01 then the q parameter will be added to the UV set 0 at that index.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.ElectricMotorScript.RpmReductionScalar
member.summary: Gets or sets the rpm reduction scalar. The purpose of this is to improve joint stability at higher RPMs by scaling down the physical rpm/angular velocity of the physics body connected to the motor, while still reporting normal RPMs via . The values range from 0-1, where zero would be complete reduction down to zero rpm, and 1 would not reduce RPM at all.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.Eva.EvaScript.CollisionInfo.GeeForce
member.summary: Gets or sets the gee force that this contact is experiencing. Note: It appears that some "collision" events (which means all and 's), may comprise of many (sometimes hundreds) of collisions, each having multiple contact points. Only a small subset of those collisions may actually contain any impulse data used to calculate GeeForce...so this cannot always be relied on as currently implemented.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.Eva.EvaScript.CollisionInfo.GeeForceFromGravity
member.summary: Gets or sets the gee force from gravity that is actively pusing this contact point into the surface it is contacting. Range is 0...1. For example, if we're doing a loop and at the top of the loop we are experiencing 5Gs, then non of that 5G is applied by gravity. Note: I realizy that it would be 6G if not for gravity "subtracting" 1G at the gop of the loop, but that is not what this property is tracking.
member.value: The gee force from gravity that is actively pusing this contact point into the surface it is contacting

member.summary: The curve used to determine the cross section scale of vertices when building the mesh. The input is the vertex depth (Y coordinate), and the output is a 0 to 1, which indicates what percentage of the scale is computed from the rear scale versus the front scale. member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.LandingGear.ConfigurableGearScript
member.summary: This script handles initializing/operating , , and sound for a wheel/landing gear with optional animated suspension (). It operates on a "fully constructed" landing gear, ie it does not bother with applying different "styles" of landing gear, or loading new prefabs representing gear types, etc. It uses scripts () to identify the important transforms it expects to be present. This class was created to de-couple the collider/animation/track renderer/sound concepts/etc. from any particular part implementation (such as ).
member.remarks: This script is currently applied directly to the landing gear prefab, and is not dynamically added.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.LandingGear.ConfigurableGearScript.RecalculateFrameState(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Called when a modifier should recalulate the reference frame sate (position/velocity) of any special, "unmanaged" game-objects.
member.remarks: Any children of a craft should have their position updated without using the position delta. However, any rigid-body other than the one associated with a will need its velocity updated with the velocity delta. Any gameobject not under a craft should add both the position and velocity deltas to the current value to keep the same relative state. - Caution: This may be called either when the reference frame recenters, rotates, or when the node's orbit position/velocity is manually updated such as while warping. If subscribing to , do not also add deltas in response to that or they'll be added in twice.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.LandingGear.LandingGearScript.RecalculateFrameState(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Called when a modifier should recalulate the reference frame sate (position/velocity) of any special, "unmanaged" game-objects.
member.remarks: Any children of a craft should have their position updated without using the position delta. However, any rigid-body other than the one associated with a will need its velocity updated with the velocity delta. Any gameobject not under a craft should add both the position and velocity deltas to the current value to keep the same relative state. - Caution: This may be called either when the reference frame recenters, rotates, or when the node's orbit position/velocity is manually updated such as while warping. If subscribing to , do not also add deltas in response to that or they'll be added in twice.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.ParachuteScript.RecalculateFrameState(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Called when a modifier should recalulate the reference frame sate (position/velocity) of any special, "unmanaged" game-objects.
member.remarks: Any children of a craft should have their position updated without using the position delta. However, any rigid-body other than the one associated with a will need its velocity updated with the velocity delta. Any gameobject not under a craft should add both the position and velocity deltas to the current value to keep the same relative state. - Caution: This may be called either when the reference frame recenters, rotates, or when the node's orbit position/velocity is manually updated such as while warping. If subscribing to GameViewScript.ReferenceFrameRecentered event, do not also add deltas in response to that or they'll be added in twice.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.PropellerAssemblyScript.CalculatePerBladeAlpha(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Calculates alpha value each blade should have to produce the desired combined transparency of stacked (blurred) blades, given all blades are stacked directly on top of each-other. Note: The blades for blur spread apart as RPM increases, and are therefore not always stacked, but when the blades are barely spread at lower RPMs we want to achieve precise "stacked transparency" values ensure it isn't too transparent at lower RPMs.
member.returns: The alpha value each blade should have.

member.summary: The dimensions of the propeller physics if its transform world scale is Vector3.one. Note: This should typically create a bounding box which matches prop mesh, but does not mean "What is the size of the mesh if the mesh had a world-scale Vector3.one". It should be the world dimensions of desired "box" which would tightly fit around the propeller if the prop mesh's parent is at a world scale of Vector3.one (prop meshes typically have local transform scales to normalize them in some way after being exported from 3d modeling programs).

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.Propulsion.RocketEngineScript.UpdateNozzleGlow(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Drives the nozzle glow. The wall temperature integrates a heat balance (throttle-driven input versus radiative and conductive cooling) so it settles at a per-nozzle equilibrium, while a separate inner-wall glow tracks exhaust intensity (mass flow per throat radius) and can run far hotter than the wall. Both are exposed via .
member.param: The engine's adjusted throttle this frame.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.ResizableWheelScript.RecalculateFrameState(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Called when a modifier should recalulate the reference frame sate (position/velocity) of any special, "unmanaged" game-objects.
member.remarks: Any children of a craft should have their position updated without using the position delta. However, any rigid-body other than the one associated with a will need its velocity updated with the velocity delta. Any gameobject not under a craft should add both the position and velocity deltas to the current value to keep the same relative state. - Caution: This may be called either when the reference frame recenters, rotates, or when the node's orbit position/velocity is manually updated such as while warping. If subscribing to GameViewScript.ReferenceFrameRecentered event, do not also add deltas in response to that or they'll be added in twice.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Craft.Parts.Modifiers.TestPilotScript.RecalculateFrameState(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Called when a modifier should re-calculate the reference frame sate (position/velocity) of any special, "unmanaged" game-objects.
member.remarks: Any children of a craft should have their position updated without using the position delta. However, any rigid-body other than the one associated with a will need its velocity updated with the velocity delta. Any gameobject not under a craft should add both the position and velocity deltas to the current value to keep the same relative state. - Caution: This may be called either when the reference frame re-centers, rotates, or when the node's orbit position/velocity is manually updated such as while warping. If subscribing to GameViewScript.ReferenceFrameRecentered event, do not also add deltas in response to that or they'll be added in twice.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Design.DesignerCraftLoader.LoadCraftInteractive(System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.String,System.Action{Assets.Scripts.Craft.CraftScript},System.Action)
member.summary: Loads the craft with the specified ID. This may be an interactive process, with message dialogs or errors being shown before completing. As such, the craft may not be loaded immediately. In fact, the craft may not be loaded at all due to errors or cancellation. The success callback will be invoked if the craft was loaded successfully (not necessarily without issues though). The failure callback will be invoked for any show-stopping errors that were encountered or if the loading was canceled.
member.param: A value indicating whether an undo step should be created when the craft is loaded.
A value indicating whether the camera should be centered on the craft when it is loaded.
The designer UI message to display (if any) when the craft is loaded.

member.summary: Removes the symmetry from the specified parts by completely removing the associated symmetry group(s). member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Design.Tutorial.PartNames
member.summary: Stable identifiers for the designer parts the stock tutorials touch.
member.remarks: Since the part-preset localization pass, every stock DesignerPart.Name is the locale key authored in its prefab/XML (e.g. DesignerParts.Fuselage1.FuelTank.Name). The tutorial layer needs a stable handle to look these parts up () and to identify them inside the partially-built tutorial craft (); both lookups compare against the raw locale key, so the constants here mirror it. The English strings ship in Strings.xml and surface through .

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.CustomWheelCollider.ResizableWheelColliderNew.RecalculateFrameState(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Called when a modifier should recalulate the reference frame sate (position/velocity) of any special, "unmanaged" game-objects.
member.remarks: Any children of a craft should have their position updated without using the position delta. However, any rigid-body other than the one associated with a will need its velocity updated with the velocity delta. Any gameobject not under a craft should add both the position and velocity deltas to the current value to keep the same relative state. - Caution: This may be called either when the reference frame recenters, rotates, or when the node's orbit position/velocity is manually updated such as while warping. If subscribing to , do not also add deltas in response to that or they'll be added in twice.

member.remarks: Counting steps rather than frames spends the benchmark's time where each craft's cost actually is. member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.ActivateActivationGroups(Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.CraftNode)
member.summary: Turns on every activation group the craft uses, so the capture exercises the parts a player would have running - bay doors, gear, lights, rcs, rotators - instead of only the engines.
member.remarks: A group holding a part that separates on activation is skipped: a detacher or interstage firing mid-capture sheds a stage, so the frames after it measure a different craft. The check is by modifier rather than by a per-craft list, so crafts added to the benchmark later are covered too. Detachers respect their DetachOnActivated flag and fairings their FairingBase flag, since only those configurations separate; docking ports merely arm on activation, but are skipped anyway rather than have the benchmark depend on that staying true.
member.returns: The report line naming what was activated and what was skipped.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.ActivateFirstStage(Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.CraftNode)
member.summary: Activates the first stage's parts, withholding the ones that separate on activation.
member.remarks: The same filter the activation groups get: a detacher, interstage or fairing firing at ignition blows pieces off the craft, and even a decorative pop destabilizes a large craft enough that the frames after it measure a rattled craft instead of the loaded one. Activating the rest of the stage part by part keeps the engines burning, which is the point of the phase.
member.returns: The report line naming what was activated and what was withheld.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.CaptureOriginShift(System.String)
member.summary: Forces a reference-frame recenter and reports the notify pass, the frame it lands in and the garbage it churns. Run intact and again on the debris field, where far more objects rebase.
member.remarks: A single recenter is enough: repeats agreed to within 2% on the craft that costs the most, so the wide run-to-run spread the older reports showed came from the editor session, not from the shift. Two probes bracket it. The backlog flush pushes whatever transform writes the preceding frames left pending, so the shift is billed only its own work. The nudge then moves the craft a millimetre and syncs that: it dirties exactly the same transforms the recenter does, so if the cost is pushing poses into physics the two match, and if it is what moving kilometres does to the broadphase, the nudge is cheap and the recenter is not.
member.param: The label identifying which origin shift this is.
member.returns: The enumerator for the coroutine.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.CollectSceneRigidbodies
member.summary: Collects the rigidbodies of every craft in the flight scene, player craft and debris alike.
member.remarks: A recenter rebases the whole scene, and a split moves bodies out from under the craft they were loaded with, so anything scoped to the player craft's transform tree measures a shrinking fraction of the work as a run goes on. Walking the craft nodes' assemblies instead is immune to how the transforms happen to be parented.
member.returns: The rigidbodies, empty when the scene has none.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.MeasureParentNudgeSync
member.summary: Measures moving each craft's root transform one millimetre, which carries every body with it.
member.remarks: This is the move an origin shift really wants: the whole craft translates and nothing changes relative to anything else. Physics only needs each actor's pose updated, and the shapes beneath them keep the local poses they already had. Whether Unity works that out or re-derives every shape anyway is the difference between a recenter costing one write per craft and one per collider, and it decides whether the parent move can stay on the transform path.
member.returns: The milliseconds the move and sync took, or 0 when there were no crafts.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.CollectActiveColliders(UnityEngine.Rigidbody,System.Collections.Generic.List{UnityEngine.Collider})
member.summary: Adds the colliders physics actually holds for a body; only those cost anything to re-pose.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.CountActiveColliders(UnityEngine.Rigidbody)
member.summary: Counts the colliders physics holds for a body.
member.returns: The collider count.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.MeasureNudgeSync(System.Collections.Generic.List{UnityEngine.Rigidbody},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Measures moving every body in the scene one millimetre and getting that into physics.
member.remarks: A millimetre cannot disturb anything spatially, so comparing this against the recenter's own sync separates pushing poses into physics from whatever moving a long way does to the broadphase. The two routes then separate the next question. Writing the body's transform invalidates every descendant, so the sync has to re-derive each collider's pose relative to its actor; writing Rigidbody.position sets the actor pose directly and never touches the hierarchy. If the transform route is far more expensive, the descendant walk is the cost even though nothing in the craft moved relative to its body. Positions are snapshotted and written back rather than offset twice, so no float error accumulates, and nothing yields while the scene is displaced.
member.param: If true, move through Rigidbody.position instead of the transform.
member.returns: The milliseconds the move and sync took, or 0 when there were no bodies.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.BuildColliderCensusLines(System.String)
member.summary: Builds the collider census for an origin shift, describing how the scene's colliders are distributed over rigidbodies and over space.
member.remarks: Two candidate drivers of a sync are measured here. Colliders per rigidbody covers the compound case, where one actor owning thousands of shapes has to re-pose all of them whenever it moves. Occupancy covers the packing case, where overlapping bounds create broadphase pairs - including pairs the craft has told physics to ignore, since that filtering happens after the broadphase. Occupancy is counted on a grid sized to the median collider rather than by testing pairs, so the census stays linear on huge craft.
member.param: The label identifying which origin shift this is.
member.returns: The census lines.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.BuildGpuCalibrationLine
member.summary: Counts the scene's active renderers by type, with material identity and property block use.
member.remarks: Draw calls scale with renderers times lighting passes, and batching dies on material identity and per-renderer state; the census turns those from suspicions into counts.
member.returns: The census line.
member.summary: Times a fixed GPU blit workload so a sweep can tell a degraded GPU state from slower render code. The blit shader ships with Unity, so nothing on the branch can change what this runs.
member.returns: The GPU calibration report line.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.BuildCalibrationLine
member.summary: Times a fixed arithmetic workload so a sweep can tell a slower machine from slower code. Nothing on the branch can change what this runs, so any movement across commits is the host.
member.returns: The calibration report line.

member.summary: Names the part types owning trigger colliders.
member.remarks: A trigger costs broadphase and narrowphase work and produces nothing the solver uses, so the part types responsible are worth naming.

member.summary: Counts the craft's flight programs, their threads and the instructions they executed last frame.
member.remarks: The type profiler bills FlightProgramScript as one number, but the cost scales with how many programs run and how much of their per-frame instruction budget each burns; naming the hungry programs turns a scene-wide cost into specific parts.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.BuildPhysicsLoadLine(System.String)
member.summary: Counts the scene's rigidbodies against the craft's own, and the part collisions being filtered.
member.remarks: Every rigidbody is an actor in the contact graph, and the shuttle reports roughly twice as many as its craft has bodies, so the remainder is worth naming. The filtered pair count says how much of the craft's own adjacency physics has been told to ignore - the utility only ignores pairs that overlap when the craft is built, so parts that merely end up touching are not in it.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.BuildColliderOutlierLine(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.List{UnityEngine.Collider})
member.summary: Names the colliders sitting furthest from the rest of the scene.
member.remarks: The census reported craft bounds spanning astronomical distances after a breakup, which means at least one collider is nowhere near the others. Whether that is debris genuinely thrown that far or a transform left holding garbage, the part has to be named before it can be judged, and a broadphase stretched over that range would cost the whole scene dearly either way. The reference point is the median of the centres so that the outliers cannot drag it towards themselves.
member.param: The label identifying which origin shift this is.
member.returns: The outlier line.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.CraftLoadProfilerScript.BuildBiggestBodyLine(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.List{UnityEngine.Collider})
member.summary: Names the part types owning the colliders on the scene's largest rigidbody.
member.remarks: A part whose sub-assembly is actuated from code has to keep those colliders as their own transforms under the body, so they cannot collapse into the compound at a fixed pose. If one actor carries thousands of shapes, this says which parts put them there, which turns a physics problem into a part-authoring one.
member.param: The label identifying which origin shift this is.
The colliders on the largest rigidbody.
member.returns: The attribution line.

member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.DebugScripts.FramePhaseAllocationSampler
member.summary: Splits each frame's managed allocation across the segments of the Unity player loop, so garbage allocated outside the craft game loop can still be attributed to a phase.
member.remarks: This component samples at the START of the update and late update phases (it sorts before every ordinary script) and its tail companion samples at the END of each, so a phase total covers the scripts between them rather than an arbitrary slice. Rendering is bracketed separately through the camera render callbacks. Frames interrupted by a collection are dropped, since the heap delta is meaningless across one. Unity's Mono stubs GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread to zero, so this reads heap size: it under-reports (allocation the heap already had room for is invisible) and must not be compared against the frame's own exact garbage total.

member.summary: The managed heap size at the previous sample point.

member.summary: The collection count at the previous sample point.

member.summary: Whether a collection has invalidated the frame currently being sampled.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Flight.GameView.Cameras.FirstPersonCameraController.EyeballOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance in meters from the center of the head to the eyeballs. When this is used, the camera no-longer simply rotates around an axis, but rather rotates around a point at a distance of . With this (along with ), the camera can be kept outside, and always looking away from the head's mesh. It makes it so we don't need to have a headless character to allow first person views while the character is still rendered.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Flight.GameView.Cameras.FirstPersonCameraController.Update(System.Int32)
member.summary: Updates the camera.
member.param: The count for this camera update frame. If this is the first update in this frame, this will be 1. If this is the second update in this frame, the count will be 2 and so on. member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Flight.GameView.ReEntry.ReEntryGlowImageEffect
member.summary: Re-entry image effect for parts. It works by: 1. Invokes a shader to create a mask of the parts currently on the screen. 2. The mask texture is then fed into an image effect shader which tints the parts with an HDR value. 3. The tinted mask is ran through a "directional bloom" image effect to create which blurs/blooms along the velocity vector. 4. The final value is naturally bloomed further by the Beautify image effect. Note: This image effect must come before the bloom effect on the camera or else it will just tint the parts...won't be any bloom.

member.summary: Sets the pinned state, which is a value indicating whether an orbital period for the target is pinned, and we're only searching for closest encounters within that period. When it is set to true, the current closest encounter's orbital period for the target is used as the pinned period. This is used when a user is trying to dial in on a specific encounter and no-longer wants the closest encounter swapped out for a closer one. They want to work w/the maneuver nodes to get a specific encounter.

member.summary: Gets the effective apoapsis distance for this orbit. For elliptical orbits, this will be the same as . For hyperbolic orbits, this will be the value returned when the distance is calculated for . For hyperbolics, the true distance is infinity, but due to precision anything beyond will result in precision issues...things will begin to equate to equal when they should not be, things will begin to fail to converge, etc. Note: This is not a guaranteed "safe" distance...it is still far as hell out, and may run into issues.
member.value: The effective apoapsis distance for this orbit.

members.member:
Gets the theoretical ceiling for the true anomaly of this orbit if it is hyperbolic. Hyperbolic orbits have a true anomaly limit that they approach, but never obtain, nor cross since hyperbolic orbits never complete a circle. If the true anomaly is set to this value, the position/velocity/time would go to infinity, so it should be used as a non-inclusive ceiling/limit. For elliptical orbits it will be NaN and should be ignored.
The maximum valid true anomaly for this orbit.
Use for the maximum true anomaly value that this orbit should ever be set to.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.MapViewManagerScript.ModApi#Flight#Sim#IGameTime#WaveTime
member.summary: Gets the time which should be used to animate wave physics/shaders. We can't just send in the float value of the current game-time b/c too much precision will be lost when get get large game-time values (like in the years). This method keeps the time within the frequency of the planet's waves. It will always be between zero and the wave frequency.
member.value: The time which should be used to animate wave physics/shaders.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.Orbits.Chain.OrbitChainNodeScript.GetTimeToNode(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Gets the time to maneuver node.
member.param: if set to true then will get the full time to the node, which is the time from the ship's current position to this node...includeing any nodes in between, otherwise it just returns the time from the parent node's position to the beginning of this node.
if set to true the absolute game time is returned (seconds to the node, plus the current time), otherwise the seconds in future.
member.returns: The time to this maneuver node.
member.remarks: You can only get the absolute time to a node if you are also getting the full time. It wouldn't make sense to get the absolute time of a single node.
member.example: GetTimeToNode(true, true) // Game time that node will start (doesn't change between calls unless burn/node changes). GetTimeToNode(true, false) // Seconds in future that node will start ("countdown"). GetTimeToNode(false, false) // Time in seconds from previous node (doesn't change between calls unless burn/node changes). GetTimeToNode(false, true) // Invalid usage.

member.name: F:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.Orbits.DrawModes.Interfaces.IDrawMode.ModeType.ParentAtReferenceTime
member.summary: Draws points relative to their parent at the parent orbit's "reference time". The reference time is whatever time is currently stored in the parent's Orbit. For "normal" objects, this should be the game's current time. For maneuver nodes/encounters, it will be when the maneuver node/encounter occurs along the orbit.

member.name: F:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.Orbits.DrawModes.Interfaces.IDrawMode.ModeType.ParentAtPointTime
member.summary: Draws points relative to the solar system center. It calculates the parent's true solar position for every point along the orbit, so is expensive to calculate. This mode results in orbits having wavy lines in the solar direction of their parents orbit, or just a regular elliptical orbit if their parent is the sun. Note: If it followed the naming convention of other modes, it could be called ParentAtIndividualTime since there is no single time used for all points...it uses each point's time and uses that to determine the parents position, and therefore it's final solar position. "Solar" seemed more descriptive though..."ParentAtPointTime" doesn't tell you much.

member.name: F:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.Orbits.DrawModes.Interfaces.IDrawMode.ModeType.ParentAtCurrentTime
member.summary: Draws points relative to their parent at the game's current time. This mode will make sure that all maneuver nodes are close to the parent planet.

member.name: F:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.Orbits.MapOrbitLine._scaledLocalOrbitPointsCache
member.summary: The orbit points with local positions which have been scaled to MapView size. It is in a kind of "hybrid" state between an orbit position (since it isn't floated) and MapView (since it is scaled).
member.remarks: 1. Reduces the number of math operations when repositioning orbits which don't change orbital params often, or at all (like the planets). 2. We could use Vectrocity's point set, but we'd have to store what the parent's position/floating origin offset were at the time the points were created. Then we'd have to subtract those out (per point) before adding the changed values in (per point). It would be slower, but wouldn't require this point cache (less memory). 3. It might be worth investigating if Vectrocity now supports lines whose transform can be moved away from the origin. If so the orbit's transform could just be moved around w/o worrying about all this...but I'm sure Vectrocity does it to reduce math operations, so it would probably be a wash performance-wise, although would clean our code up. It actually might be slower if to support it, Vectrocity required an add/subtract per-point every frame as a result (to move it back to the origin), even if the line didn't change.

member.summary: Gets the orbit line position at the specified index in scaledOrbitPointsCache, and updates data related to the special "precise point" which represent's the point which is always placed at the craft's position to prevent it from moving away from lines with lower resolutions, or when deeply zoomed in. This method is only intended to be called from within MapOrbitLine.RepositionOrbitLine()"/>
member.param: The index of the requested point.
The current/updated index of precise point within scaledOrbitPointsCache. The "precise point" is the point point which follows the orbit item so that the item never "floats" off the line.
The true anomaly of the point in scaledOrbitPointsCache which comes before the requested point...this value is updated before returning.
member.returns: The position of the point requested.

member.summary: Sets the pinned state, which is a value indicating whether an orbital period for the target is pinned, and we're only searching for closest encounters within that period. When it is set to true, the current closest encounter's orbital period for the target is used as the pinned period. This is used when a user is trying to dial in on a specific encounter and no-longer wants the closest encounter swapped out for a closer one. They want to work w/the maneuver nodes to get a specific encounter.

member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Flight.MapView.UI.PhysicsRaycasterCustomScript
member.summary: This is a physics ray-caster replacement for Unity's b/c w/Unity's version, every click-able object has to be a child of the camera, which does not work for us. To get the click events which will be sent onto world objects, this physics ray-caster needs to be on a canvas component with a GraphicRaycaster. This component receives click events from the GraphicRaycaster, shoots a ray out into the world, and checks to see if items hit have implemented any of the input interfaces (IDragHandler, IPointerClickHandler, etc).

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the struct. Order of node A/B matters because an encounter searched for one period from nodeA's current position.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.ClosestEncounterSearchOptions.BinarySearchTargetDistance
member.summary: Gets or sets the binary search target distance. This is the distance under which the last binary search step will be performed. Set this to smaller than the planet's SOI to help ensure sure it wasn't "stepped over". Since this impacts the smallest step performed in the search, it also impacts the "jumpy-ness" of the closest approach icon. If SOI is being passed in, closest encounters against planets with very large SOIs may appear more jittery (although the relative precision is the same). Note: Glancing encounters may require a very small step distance to ensure an encounter isn't missed. There is no way to know ahead of time if an encounter is "glancing" or not, though so this might just need to be a performance setting.

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.ClosestEncounterSearchOptions.DebugDescription
member.summary: Gets or sets the debug description. Set to null for normal operation. If set, debug info will be shown and the description is used to make unique names for debug gizmos.

member.summary: Gets or sets the local minima modifier. The higher the number, the less chance that a local minima will be selected instead of the overall closest point. The default is 1. Note: This does not impact the apparent "resolution" of the closest point selection...i.e. it will not make the closest approach icon jump around less. The value that impacts that is the .

member.name: P:Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.Orbit.ApoapsisDistanceEffective
member.summary: Gets the effective apoapsis distance for this orbit. For elliptical orbits, this will be the same as . For hyperbolic orbits, this will be the distance when the distance is calculated for . For hyperbolics, the true distance is infinity, but due to precision anything beyond will result in precision issues...things will begin to equate to equal when they should not be, things will begin to fail to converge, etc. Note: This is not a guaranteed "safe" distance...it is still far as hell out, and may run into issues.
member.value: The effective apoapsis distance for this orbit.

member.summary: Gets the eccentricity vector.

members.member:
Gets the theoretical ceiling for the true anomaly of this orbit if it is hyperbolic. Hyperbolic orbits have a true anomaly limit that they approach, but never obtain, nor cross since hyperbolic orbits never complete a circle. If the true anomaly is set to this value, the position/velocity/time would go to infinity, so it should be used as a non-inclusive ceiling/limit. For elliptical orbits it will be NaN and should be ignored.
The maximum valid true anomaly for this orbit.
is the maximum true anomaly value that this (hyperbolic) orbit should ever be set to.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.OrbitAnalyser.BinarySearch(ModApi.Flight.Sim.IOrbitNode,ModApi.Flight.Sim.IOrbitNode,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double@,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Performs a binary search for the closest positions between the two nodes using the given true anomaly range.
member.param: The distance under which the last binary search step will be performed. Set this to smaller than the planet's SOI to help ensure sure it wasn't "stepped over". Since this impacts the smallest step performed in the search, it also impacts the "jumpy-ness" of the closest approach icon. If SOI is being passed in, closest encounters against planets with very large SOIs may appear more jittery (although the relative precision is the same). Note: Glancing encounters may require a very small step distance to ensure an encounter isn't missed. There is no way to know ahead of time if an encounter is "glancing" or not, though so this might just need to be a performance setting.
The final step ea step when the search completes.
Set to null for normal operation. If set, debug info will be shown and the description is used to make unique names for debug gizmos.
Debug use only. Dictates if this binary search is on the "right" or "left" side.
member.returns: The closest point information after performing the search.

member.name: M:Assets.Scripts.Flight.Sim.OrbitAnalyser.GetAscendingDescendingNodes(ModApi.Flight.Sim.IOrbit,ModApi.Flight.Sim.IOrbit,ModApi.Flight.Sim.IOrbitPoint@,ModApi.Flight.Sim.IOrbitPoint@)
member.summary: Gets the ascending and descending nodes which lie on orbitA with respect to orbitB. These are the points where the two orbits cross, and thus where performing a normal burn will result in the orbits becoming co-planar. Note: Swapping orbitA and orbitB will result in different ascending/descending node points (the points are always on orbitA), but both pairs would all lie on the planeIntersection vector.
member.param: The orbit to determine the two points (ascending/descending nodes) at which a normal burn will result in making the orbits co-planar .
The point at which performing a normal burn will most quickly result in the two orbits becoming co-planar.
The point at which performing an anti-normal burn will most quickly result in the two orbits becoming co-planar.

member.summary: Calculates the precise points where the two body's SOIs meet, given two points where they are already inside each-other's SOI (important). Note: This method is different from OrbitMath.GetEscapePoint() in that GetEscapePoint() requires an orbit be constructed relative to the body being escaped...these orbits are relative to another, central body.
member.param: Body A's SOI. Can be zero.
Body B's SOI. Cannot be zero.
Any point where A is already inside B's SOI.
Point B at the same time as point A.

A point on orbitA which occurs prior to the points being inside. Needs to be on the same half of the orbit to properly determine if if points are on the near/far side of orbitB (so we know which soi edge side we're guaging against).
The distance between startPointA and startPointB
Mostly used for debug operations, allows recieving a callback for every iteration of the search loop.
The final point for A when the SOIs meet, just inside the intersection.
The final point for B when the SOIs meet, just inside the intersection.
member.remarks: Important: You'd typically want to pass in -stepValueThatGotUsIntoTheSoi for eaStepTowardSoiEdge or it will find the "other side's" SOI edge. Note: This method is slower than a binary search, but it is guaranteed to find the SOI w/o possibly fallinig into any local minima.

member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Flight.UI.NavSphereScript
member.summary: Script for the nav sphere. The nav sphere is aligned so that following is true: (0 pitch, 0 heading) = target is pointing along +Y (90 pitch, 0 heading) = target is pointing along +Z (-90 pitch, 0 heading) = target is pointing along -Z (0 pitch, 90 heading) = target is pointing along -X (0 pitch, +/-180 heading) = target is pointing along -Y (0 pitch, 270/-90 heading) = target is pointing along +X

member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.State.GameStateManager
member.summary: Provides methods to manage game states. Game states are organized in the following manner: /UserData/GameStates/{GameStateId}/{Tag} The {GameStateId} folder contains a set of game states, with different tags. The current game state for the set is tagged Active. More tags may be used when the player makes a quicksave or when a checkpoint is saved prior to the player launching. For example, with a game state ID of ABC123, the path structure would look like this: /UserData/GameStates/ABC123/Active /UserData/GameStates/ABC123/QuickSave /UserData/GameStates/ABC123/PreFlight

member.name: T:Assets.Scripts.Terrain.Rendering.PlanetCloudRenderer
member.summary: Builds and updates the detached (fake) cloud spheres for a planet rendered in scaled space. This is shared by every context that renders a planet from space (flight, map view, main menu, planet studio) so the cloud rendering lives in one place. A world-scale ground variant renders the same spheres for the close-up view. It is driven entirely by the planet's rendering data, so it has no dependency on any single scene's singletons.

member.param: The transform to move and use for orientation.

The accumulated delta from previous calls when not enough moment had occurred to snap to the next place on the grid. On the initial call, this would be Vector3.zero. Then the result of each subsequent call would be feed back into the call to drag.
Size of the grid. Set to zero for smooth movement.
If set to true the transform local orientation is used, otherwise world orientation is used.
member.returns: The delta accumulated from this call when there was not enough movement to snap to a new position....it used for successive calls to Drag (snapDeltaAccum parameter).
member.exception: dragDir must be Vector3.up/right/forward when world grid snapping is used.

Used to add non-default attributes to this element in the XSD file It is only necessary to override this if your custom tag handler provides new attributes and you wish for Visual Studio to autocomplete them for you. The key is the name of the attribute, and the value is the datatype. The datatype must be a valid datatype within XmlLayout.xsd or http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema e.g. xs:string -> string value (from http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema) xs:integer -> integer value (from http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema) xs:float -> float value (from http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema) xmlLayout:color -> color in hex/rgb/rgba format xmlLayout:vector2 -> vector 2 in x y format xmlLayout:floatList -> list of floats e.g. "10 10 10"
